newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sembawang Corp proposes merger with JSL.
newsitem.headline: Sembawang Corp proposes merger with JSL.

text.p: Sembawang Corp has proposed merging its shipyard-related and offshore engineering business with Jurong Shipyard Ltd (JSL), Sembawang's financial adviser for the proposed merger said.

Standard Chartered Merchant Bank Asia Ltd said in a statement late on Friday that Sembawang would inject Singapore $279.28 million worth of its assets into JSL in exchange for some 41.07 million new JSL shares.
This would raise Sembawang's interest in JSL to 41.6 percent from 20 percent, the statement said.
The new JSL shares are valued at S$6.80 each, representing a 10.5 percent discount to the last transacted price of S$7.50 of JSL shares on Friday.

The proposed merger would be effected by way of a conditional put and call option agreement, under which Sembawang would have the right to ask JSL to acquire, and JSL would have the right to require Sembawang to transfer the assets.

The statement said Sembawang's directors believed the merger would allow the enlarged JSL to operate about 1.71 million deadweight tonnes of docking capacity, constituting about half the total docking capacity of Singapore's four major shipyards.

It said the merger would also give JSL access to a larger pool of manpower and to Sembawang's ship-repair operations in Indonesia, China and the Middle East and its offshore engineering operations in China, Malaysia and Indonesia.

The proposed merger would only be completed in 1997 and would therefore have no effect on Sembawang's earnings per share and net tangible assets per share for the financial year ending December 31, 1996.
The statement said the proposed merger was subject to the approval of shareholders of both companies, regulatory authorities and certain Sembawang joint venture partners.
